newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Mayora sees 1996 sales up to 335 bln rph.
newsitem.headline: Mayora sees 1996 sales up to 335 bln rph.

text.p: Indonesia's snack food manufacturer PT Mayora Indah said on Monday it expected its 1996 net sales to rise to 335 billion rupiah from 305 billion rupiah in 1995.

"We expect to book net sales of 335 billion rupiah in 1996. In 1995 we booked around 305 billion rupiah. The rises were partly due to strong sales from our coffee and cocoa processing divisions," corporate secretary Andi Laurus told Reuters.
Laurus declined to give the firm's expected net profit in 1996, saying Mayora's full year 1996 financial results were still being counted.
Laurus also said demand was strong ahead of the coming Eid al-Fitr Moslem celebrations, but he did not give details.
Meanwhile, Laurus denied market talk that its factory in the western Javanese town of Bandung was damaged by its workers.
"The rumour is baseless. We do not have any factory in Bandung. Our factory is located in Tangerang," Laurus said.
Tangerang is an industrial region bordering Jakarta.
Laurus said the rumour was possibly sparked by news reports that a major textile factory at Bandung, some 200 km from Jakarta, was damaged by its workers during an alleged bonus dispute last week.
Mayora was among the most active stocks in early trading. It rose 25 rupiah to 1,050 rupiah.
